items.headline: August core PCE cools to 3.0% y/y (vs 3.3% expected); October rate-hike odds collapse from ~72% to ~35%
items.summary: The Fed's preferred inflation gauge rose 0.2% m/m and 3.0% y/y in August, undershooting the 3.3% consensus, even as headline PCE held near 3.4% on a 4.4% jump in gasoline prices tied to the Iran war, and real consumer spending rose a strong 0.6%. The softer core print sent market-implied odds of an October 28 Fed hike tumbling to roughly 35% (from Tuesday's ~72.5% peak), though odds of at least one more hike by December remain near 80% given the Fed's hawkish September dot plot.
items.actionable: The drop in October hike odds should ease the real-yields drag that has weighed on the silver/miner sleeve all week, but December odds near 80% mean the position isn't out of the woods -- Friday's payrolls (consensus ~85-90k, down from August's 162k) is the next binary catalyst.

items.headline: Gold and silver's PCE-day rally fizzles as the dollar rips higher despite cooler inflation -- gold back near $4,150-4,167, silver retraces to $60.84
items.summary: Gold and silver initially jumped on the softer core PCE print Wednesday morning -- silver touched $61.73 -- but the dollar reversed higher against every major currency except the pound by the afternoon, dragging gold back to roughly $4,150-4,167/oz (GLD -0.54% in the portfolio spine) and silver down to the 50% retracement of its all-time high near $60.84 (SLV -1.75%). FXStreet and TheGoldForecast attributed the reversal to the same report's strong 0.6% real consumer-spending growth, which supported the dollar even as the disinflation narrative and bond yields eased.
items.actionable: The 'good inflation news, bad dollar reaction' pattern is the specific mechanism behind Wednesday's SLV/GLD declines in the price spine -- it means the silver/miner sleeve is now trading off dollar strength as much as real yields, so Friday's payrolls matters for the dollar leg too, not just the rate-hike-odds leg.

items.headline: Brent-WTI spread blows out to widest since May: Gulf export recovery hits Brent while a possible Trump diesel-export ban props up WTI
items.summary: Middle East crude exports hit their highest level since the Iran war began as Saudi Arabia fully restored Red Sea pipeline and Yanbu-terminal loadings, pulling the Brent-linked geopolitical risk premium out of the market (Brent fell ~2.6% to $102.59 Tuesday, with the portfolio spine showing a further thin-volume slide Wednesday). WTI decoupled and held firmer because President Trump said September 30 he is still 'thinking about' restricting US diesel exports to fight $6.45+/gallon pump prices -- a step that would force more domestic crude into US refining -- pushing the Brent-WTI spread to roughly $12/barrel, its widest since May, even as Trump signaled he was cooling on an outright ban given the risk of higher gasoline prices.
items.actionable: This is a US-refining-policy story layered on a genuine Gulf-supply recovery, not a demand shock -- it explains the week's Brent/WTI split without implying a fresh oil-demand-driven risk-off move, so it shouldn't be read as a new headwind for the silver/miner inflation-hedge thesis the way a real demand collapse would be.

items.headline: Trump-Xi summit extends the rare-earth export-control truce to January 10, 2027, but MP Materials keeps rallying on Pentagon/magnet-campus news, not the truce
items.summary: Treasury Secretary Bessent confirmed the US-China trade truce -- covering China's suspended rare-earth export controls originally set to expire November 10, 2026 -- has been extended roughly two months to January 10, 2027 following the Trump-Xi summit; CSIS analysts noted the shorter-than-expected extension 'suggests the US is unsatisfied with China's offers.' Separately, MP Materials rose another ~5.8% Wednesday (Sept 30, consistent with the portfolio spine's +4.09%) on company-specific news -- a $1.25bn+-backed North Texas magnet campus, a 10-year Pentagon offtake, and a Freedom Broker Hold initiation with a $57 target -- showing the stock is increasingly trading on Western defense-demand fundamentals rather than the China scarcity-premium narrative.
items.actionable: The truce extension removes the near-term Nov-10 supply-shock catalyst that was the structural bull case's pillar, but MP's continued strength on Pentagon/magnet-campus news suggests the ex-China watchlist can still work on a defense-demand thesis even as the trade-war scarcity premium compresses -- worth distinguishing the two drivers position by position.

items.headline: Hang Seng opens Golden-Week-eve session down ~0.5% to 24,393 as Beijing's DeepSeek/Moonshot data-security probe (tied to Anthropic's Claude) keeps weighing on China AI names
items.summary: The Hang Seng Index fell 129 points (0.52%) to 24,393 at Wednesday's open, with Tencent down 0.4% and Xiaomi little changed, extending a September pattern where HK tech has traded nervously on both the US real-yields shock and a homegrown AI overhang. That overhang traces to a September 23 report that China's Cyberspace Administration opened a probe into whether AI startups DeepSeek and Moonshot routed live user data through Anthropic's Claude, which knocked the HSI below 25,000 (-1.01% to 24,834) and hit Alibaba (-4.4%) and Xiaomi (-3.8%) hardest that day. Mainland China now shuts for the week-long October 1-7 Golden Week, compressing HK-tech-driven flow for the rest of the week.
items.actionable: The AI-bubble/data-security overhang is now a second, homegrown risk factor for the 0700/0981/1810 sleeve on top of the US real-yields story, and with mainland China closed for Golden Week the position is more exposed to lower-liquidity, HK-only swings on either theme through Oct 7.

items.headline: STI closes Q3 2026 up 22.9% YTD -- one of its strongest years on record -- but S-REITs sit 8.2% in the red as banks carry the rally
items.summary: The Straits Times Index opened firmer Wednesday despite a weak Wall Street lead, closing out Q3 2026 up 22.9% year-to-date (roughly triple its historical 5-7% annual average) on the strength of DBS and OCBC and Singapore's AI-driven capex boom, per The Kopi Notes' Q3 wrap published September 30. The FTSE ST All-Share REIT Index has badly lagged, down 8.2% over the same period as the Fed's rate hikes to 3.75-4.00% pressured REIT valuations and competed with fixed income, even though underlying REIT distributions have actually grown.
items.actionable: The bank/REIT divergence this quarter (STI +22.9% vs S-REITs -8.2%) supports staying overweight DBS/OCBC/Singtel and underweight Keppel REIT into the October MAS Monetary Policy Statement (due by Oct 14) -- a tightening surprise (45% of forecasters expect one) would likely extend, not reverse, that split.

items.headline: Houthi threat to Aramco's Yanbu hub and stalled US-Iran Hormuz talks remain unresolved even as Gulf export volumes hit war-era highs
items.summary: Yemen's Houthis' September 25 claimed strikes on Saudi Aramco's Yanbu hub and a Riyadh-area target (intercepted by Saudi air defenses) prompted France to commit troops, radars and defense systems to protect the site. As of the September 29-30 oil-market wires, US-Iran talks over the Strait of Hormuz remain stalled even as Saudi Arabia has fully restored Yanbu/Red Sea pipeline flows and September Middle East crude exports hit their highest level since the war began -- the gap between record exports flowing now and unresolved blockade/attack risk is why Goldman still frames Brent within an unusually wide $80-120 range.
items.actionable: The Houthi/Hormuz tail risk to the same Yanbu infrastructure currently pumping at record rates is unresolved, not resolved -- it's the reason to keep some inflation-hedge exposure in the silver/miner sleeve rather than treating this week's oil pullback as a full close-out of the supply-shock case.

items.headline: Bitcoin stuck in the $83-84k range as spot ETF inflows collapse from ~$1bn/day to $134m; today's XRP escrow release and the Oct 27-28 FOMC are the next catalysts
items.summary: Bitcoin has traded in an $83,000-$84,000 band since testing an eight-month high near $87,000 on September 21; US spot BTC ETFs took in a strong $2.4bn in the week to September 25 (the largest weekly haul since October 2025) before daily inflows collapsed to just $134m in the final days of the month, signaling fading momentum into October. Separately, Ripple can release up to 1 billion XRP from escrow today (October 1), a routine monthly unlock, while Ethereum's Glamsterdam upgrade is due its first public testnet on October 6.
items.actionable: With Bitcoin trading in lockstep with the same real-yields/dollar narrative driving gold and silver this week rather than offering a hedge, and ETF demand now fading, there's no diversification case for adding to the crypto sleeve ahead of the Oct 27-28 FOMC -- that meeting, not today's routine XRP unlock, is the real catalyst.

items.headline: China's Golden Week (Oct 1-7) begins today with PBOC gold buying at a 2023-high pace, a structural counterweight to this week's dollar-driven pullback
items.summary: The People's Bank of China added 20.2 tonnes of gold in August, its largest monthly purchase since October 2023, per World Gold Council data, extending a central-bank bid that has cushioned every 2026 dip. China's week-long Golden Week holiday begins today (October 1) and traditionally marks the start of peak seasonal local gold-buying, a potential source of fresh physical demand into a market that has otherwise traded off the dollar and real yields this week.
items.actionable: The PBOC bid and the Golden Week demand window are the slower-moving structural support underpinning the silver/miner sleeve even through Wednesday's dollar-driven pullback -- worth distinguishing this from the day-to-day dollar/real-yields noise when deciding whether to add on weakness.

items.headline: September nonfarm payrolls due Friday Oct 2, consensus ~85-90k (BofA sees just 60k) versus August's 162k -- the next binary catalyst after Wednesday's soft PCE
items.summary: The BLS releases the September jobs report Friday at 8:30am ET (evening SGT), with consensus around 85-90k (range 35k-180k) versus August's 162k gain and unemployment expected to hold at 4.1%. Bank of America's below-consensus 60k call flags the slowdown as partly seasonal-factor payback from an unusually strong August rather than genuine hiring deterioration.
items.actionable: This is the next scheduled catalyst that could re-price the whole book within 48 hours -- a soft print would extend Wednesday's rates relief (good for silver/miners, HK tech and SGX banks via lower discount rates), while a hot print could revive the hawkish-Fed/dollar-strength dynamic that hurt gold and silver on PCE day itself.

note: 10 items published; 6 of 10 dated 29 Sep-1 Oct, satisfying the freshness bar (running Thu 1 Oct pre-Asia-open, as of Wed 30 Sep US close). Two planned items were dropped after verification failed (a purported Q3 DBS/OCBC/UOB earnings story turned out to be a forward-looking editorial, not actual results; a 'CGSI switches into S-REITs' call turned out to be dated March 2025) -- both excluded rather than included on stale/misattributed grounds.
